title: Post-CABG (Cardiac Surgery) Discharge Summary
raw_text:
PATIENT: Robert Miller, 64M. ADMISSION DATE: Oct 12. DISCHARGE DATE: Oct 18.
HOSPITAL: St. Jude Heart & Vascular Institute. ATTENDING: Dr. Angela Vance, MD (Cardiothoracic Surgery).

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: Status-post coronary artery bypass grafting x3 (LIMA-LAD, SVG-OM1, SVG-RCA) for 3-vessel CAD.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Aspirin 81 mg oral tablet daily with breakfast indefinitely.
2. Metoprolol Tartrate 25 mg oral tablet twice daily (morning and evening) with meals. Monitor heart rate.
3. Atorvastatin 40 mg oral tablet once daily at bedtime.
4. Furosemide (Lasix) 20 mg oral tablet once daily in the morning for 14 days.
5. Take pain medication as needed for chest wall discomfort.

APPOINTMENTS & FOLLOW-UP:
1. Follow-up with Dr. Vance in Cardiothoracic Surgery Clinic in 10 to 14 days for sternal wound inspection and suture assessment.
2. Follow-up with primary cardiologist Dr. Keith Chen in 3 to 4 weeks.
3. Schedule Phase II Cardiac Rehabilitation intake assessment within 4 to 6 weeks.

CARE TASKS & MONITORING:
- Weigh yourself every morning after urination and before breakfast. Call team if weight increases by >3 lbs in 24 hours or 5 lbs in a week.
- Check and record blood pressure and heart rate twice daily (morning and evening).
- Inspect sternal incision and leg vein harvest site daily for erythema, purulent drainage, or warmth.
- Perform incentive spirometry 10 breaths every hour while awake for the first week.

RESTRICTIONS & PRECAUTIONS:
- Sternal Precautions for 8 weeks: Do not lift anything over 5 pounds. Do not push or pull with arms. Avoid reaching behind your back.
- Driving restriction: Absolutely no driving for 4 weeks or while taking narcotic analgesics.
- Diet: 2-gram sodium cardiac diet with fluid restriction of 2 liters per day.

RED FLAG SYMPTOMS (CALL 911 OR VISIT EMERGENCY ROOM IMMEDIATELY):
- Crushing chest pressure or shortness of breath at rest.
- Sternal clicking or feeling of bones shifting.
- Fever above 101.5 F or severe chills.
- Rapid heart rate (>110 bpm) or irregular fluttering sensation.

title: Type 2 Diabetes & CKD Care Transition Plan
raw_text:
PATIENT: Elena Rodriguez, 58F. DISCHARGE SUMMARY.
FACILITY: Metro Community Health Center. PROVIDER: Dr. Marcus Thorne, MD.
PRIMARY DIAGNOSES: Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with acute kidney injury on Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3b, Essential Hypertension.

MEDICATION ADJUSTMENTS:
- DISCONTINUE Metformin 1000 mg BID immediately due to renal clearance concerns (eGFR 32 mL/min).
- START Insulin Glargine (Lantus) 18 units subcutaneous injection once daily at bedtime.
- Insulin Lispro (Humalog) 4 units subcutaneous injection with major meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner).
- Lisinopril 10 mg oral tablet once daily in the morning. Recheck renal panel and potassium in 10 days.
- Empagliflozin (Jardiance) temporarily held until nephrology clearance.

MONITORING & TESTING TASKS:
- Check blood sugar regularly.
- Keep log of all glucose readings and bring to next clinic visit.
- Log daily morning blood pressure. Target systolic < 130 mmHg.
- Fasting Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and urine microalbumin lab draw on Day 10.

FOLLOW-UP APPOINTMENTS:
- Nephrology consultation with Dr. S. Gupta in 2 to 3 weeks for renal function evaluation.
- Diabetes Educator & Nutritionist consultation within 14 days for insulin injection technique and carbohydrate counting.
- Primary Care follow-up with Dr. Thorne in 4 weeks.

DIET & HYDRATION:
- Low potassium, low phosphorus diabetic diet. Maximum sodium 1500 mg daily. Stay adequately hydrated.

RED FLAGS TO WATCH:
- Hypoglycemia signs: shakiness, sweating, confusion, dizziness (take 15g fast-acting carbs if glucose < 70 mg/dL).
- Severe lethargy, nausea, vomiting, or persistent metallic taste.
- Blood glucose persistently above 300 mg/dL with ketones.

title: Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) Post-Op Rehab
raw_text:
PATIENT: Walter Jenkins, 71M. PROCEDURE: Right Total Knee Arthroplasty.
SURGEON: Dr. Patricia Sterling, MD, Department of Orthopedic Surgery.
DISCHARGE DATE: Day 2 post-operative.

MEDICATIONS:
1. Enoxaparin (Lovenox) 30 mg subcutaneous injection once daily for 14 days for DVT prophylaxis.
2. Celecoxib (Celebrex) 200 mg oral capsule once daily with food for anti-inflammatory pain control.
3. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) 650 mg oral tablet every 6 hours scheduled for 7 days. Do not exceed 3000 mg total acetaminophen per day.
4. Oxycodone 5 mg oral tablet 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours as needed for severe breakthrough pain only (max 4 doses per 24 hours).
5. Docusate Sodium (Colace) 100 mg oral capsule twice daily while taking opioids.

REHABILITATION & CARE TASKS:
- Home Health Physical Therapy evaluation within 48 hours of discharge, then 3 sessions per week.
- Perform home exercise program (ankle pumps, quad sets, straight leg raises) 3 sets of 10 repetitions, 3 times daily.
- Cryotherapy / Ice machine application to right knee for 20 minutes every 2 hours while awake.
- Keep surgical dressing clean, dry, and intact. Aquacel dressing in place.

APPOINTMENTS:
- Orthopedic Clinic with Physician Assistant for surgical staple removal in 12 to 14 days.
- Follow-up X-rays and surgical evaluation with Dr. Sterling in 6 weeks.

RESTRICTIONS & PRECAUTIONS:
- Weight-bearing as tolerated with front-wheeled rolling walker. Do not pivot on operative leg.
- No submerging incision in water (no tub baths, swimming, or hot tubs) until cleared by surgeon.

RED FLAG SYMPTOMS:
- Calf pain, calf swelling, or localized tenderness in either leg (suspected DVT).
- Sudden onset chest pain or shortness of breath (PE alert - call 911).
- Incision drainage that turns yellow/green or emits a foul odor.
- Inability to bend knee or severe uncontrolled pain not relieved by medication.

title: Pediatric Asthma Exacerbation Home Plan
raw_text:
PATIENT: Maya Patel, 7F. PARENT/CAREGIVER: Sunita Patel.
FACILITY: Children's Emergency Department. ATTENDING: Dr. Rebecca Ross, MD.
DIAGNOSIS: Moderate acute asthma exacerbation triggered by viral upper respiratory infection.

ASTHMA ACTION PLAN MEDICATIONS:
1. Albuterol HFA (90 mcg/puff) Inhaler: 2 puffs via spacer every 4 hours as needed for wheezing, cough, or tightness.
2. Prednisolone syrup (15 mg/5 mL): Give 10 mL (30 mg) oral liquid once daily each morning with breakfast for 5 days. Complete the full 5-day course.
3. Fluticasone Propionate (Flovent 44 mcg) Inhaler: 1 puff twice daily (morning and bedtime) via spacer. Rinse mouth with water after use to prevent thrush.

TASKS & MONITORING:
- Measure peak flow readings every morning before taking maintenance inhaler. Record in asthma journal.
- Wash spacer chamber once weekly in warm soapy water and air dry.
- Ensure child stays indoors on high pollen advisory days.

APPOINTMENTS:
- Follow-up with primary pediatrician Dr. Ross or associate within 48 to 72 hours for pulmonary reassessment.
- Pediatric Allergy & Immunology appointment in 6 weeks for formal skin testing.

RED FLAG DANGER SIGNS (CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY):
- Chest or ribs pulling in with each breath (sternal or intercostal retractions).
- Breathing so hard child cannot speak full sentences without gasping.
- Grunting, nasal flaring, or pale/blue tint around lips or fingernails.
- Albuterol inhaler relief lasts less than 3 hours.

title: Elderly Fall & Concussion Observation Plan
raw_text:
PATIENT: Harold Crawford, 82M. ADMIT: Observation Unit.
PHYSICIAN: Dr. Leonard Vance, MD. DIAGNOSIS: Mechanical ground-level fall with mild traumatic brain injury / concussion, forehead laceration (closed with Dermabond).

MEDICATIONS & DE-PRESCRIBING:
1. DISCONTINUE Zolpidem (Ambien) 5 mg immediately. Do not resume sleep medications.
2. Tylenol 500 mg oral tablet every 6 hours as needed for headache (max 2000 mg/day).
3. Continue home antihypertensive: Amlodipine 5 mg once daily in morning.
4. Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, or NSAIDs for 72 hours due to intracranial bleeding precaution.

TASKS & MONITORING:
- Caregiver must check neurological status every 4 hours while awake for 48 hours.
- Limit screen time and cognitive exertion.
- Conduct home safety walkthrough: Remove throw rugs, ensure adequate lighting, keep walker at bedside.

FOLLOW-UP APPOINTMENTS:
- Primary care provider visit in 5 to 7 days for fall risk reassessment and medication review.
- Physical therapy balance and gait assessment in 2 weeks.

RED FLAGS (GO TO NEAREST EMERGENCY ROOM):
- Repeated vomiting or worsening severe headache.
- Increased confusion, difficulty waking from sleep, or slurred speech.
- Unequal pupil size, weakness in one arm or leg, or seizure activity.
